article.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
article.summary: Nvidia research shows that AI agents can perform well, and not go off the deep end, through fine-tuning, even if the AI model isn't that great at the task.

article.title: Google is giving you more control over your shared photo location data
article.summary: Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority TL;DR Google is introducing a new Photo Picker API that allows users to choose if location data is included with the photos they share. If the user agrees to share location data with an app, they won’t be asked again for that app. Users will be able to revoke access or regrant access by tapping on the location info button in the bottom right corner of the Photo Picker UI. By default, Android’s Photo Picker strips location data (EXIF data) from the photos you choose to share with apps. While this is great for those who care deeply about privacy, certain apps rely on EXIF data (for non-invasive reasons) to function properly. article.title: ChatGPT could soon let you lock chats behind a PIN or fingerprint
article.summary: TL;DR OpenAI has been spotted working on a new feature that would let you lock your chats. Locked chats could let you hide saved ChatGPT conversations from your sidebar, history, and search results behind a PIN or fingerprint. Unlike Temporary Chats, locked chats are designed to stick around, giving users a way to save sensitive conversations without leaving them visible in their regular history. Locked chats could also create a privacy boundary for Memory, letting new information from locked conversations personalize other locked chats without spilling into regular conversations. Your ChatGPT history isn’t necessarily a record that you want to parade around.
